title: Inside the Mind of Claude AI Three.js ASCII Animation
text:
Build a single self-contained HTML file using Three.js that renders a
~150-second, fully automated, cinematic camera journey "inside the mind of
an AI". Render everything through a custom ASCII post-processing shader
(dense monospace glyph grid, characters chosen by luminance, tinted per
scene, subtle glow and film grain). No cuts — one continuous camera path
with smooth crossfades between rooms.

Scenes (in order, each with its own palette):
1. Black void with sparse drifting glyphs. Center terminal prompt "> wake _"
   with an orange (#D97757) chevron and blinking cursor.
2. Amber/gold infinite library hall — tall shelves, arches, glowing lamp,
   camera dollies forward.
3. Teal/blue towering pillars made of falling digits.
4. Purple constellation: floating words connected by lines, forming a web.
5. Grey staircase climbing upward into darkness.
6. Deep red room of noise with a single lit doorway; camera approaches it.
7. Pale/warm room where a calm face made of characters emerges.

Captions: bottom-center, lowercase, JetBrains Mono, letter-spaced, on a
soft dark gradient bar. Each line types in with a "decode" effect (random
glyphs in orange resolve into the real letters). Use this script, timed
across the scenes: [paste the captions above]

Make the timeline deterministic (driven by a time variable, not real
time) and expose window.renderFrame(t) so it can be captured frame by frame
at 1920x1080, 30fps. Add a ?record flag that hides the UI.

the rest is fine tuning the room until it looked all good

title: Maglev Train Journey Through Impossible Worlds
text:
SCENE CONTEXT
Chaotic amateur first-person phone footage shot by a standing passenger during rush hour inside a packed magnetic-levitation train that races through one violent, unbroken 30-second journey with no cuts.
The video begins immediately inside a colossal titan valley. Enormous humanoid titans hundreds of meters tall are already walking beside and across the train route. The journey then flows continuously into a prehistoric dinosaur basin, through a gigantic living jungle, upward into a futuristic megastructure suspended across the sky, through an enormous machine-city built at impossible scale, and finally into a vast artificial world where entire cities surround a contained artificial sun.
The scale continuously escalates.
The car violently heaves, snakes, drops, and banks throughout the journey. Everyone inside is tightly packed and gripping poles or straps, enduring the ride almost silently.
The phone operator grips a pole with one hand and films shakily with the other, repeatedly swinging the phone between the crowded passengers and the left-side windows as unbelievable environments rush past.
A calm public-address voice bookends the journey.
LOCATION MAP
Interior foreground:
A standing-room-only futuristic maglev commuter car.
Bodies pressed shoulder to shoulder.
Passengers gripping overhead straps and vertical poles with white knuckles.
Backpacks squeezed between bodies.
Coats and loose clothing shifting with each jolt.
A narrow central aisle completely jammed with standing commuters.
Large panoramic windows run along the LEFT side of the carriage.
The camera remains inside this exact same train car for the entire video.
The train always travels in the SAME forward direction.
Everything outside streaks past the windows front-to-back.
Exterior zones crossed in this exact continuous order:
Colossal Titan Valley.
Prehistoric dinosaur basin.
Dense gigantic prehistoric jungle.
Ascending mountain passage leading into clouds.
Enormous futuristic ring megastructure above the clouds.
Interior machine-city of impossible scale.
Artificial-world civilization surrounding a contained miniature sun.
Each zone physically connects into the next.
No teleportation.
No instant environment replacement.
No discontinuity in geography.
Camera stays inside the car at chest height.
Exterior light enters primarily from the LEFT windows.
FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
Open immediately on chaos.
At 0.0 seconds the phone is already recording.
The frame is crooked, off-center, and partially blocked by the shoulder of another standing passenger.
Foreground:
A commuter grips a vertical steel pole with both hands as the carriage violently sways.
Mid-ground:
Three passengers white-knuckle overhead straps.
Their bodies all lean simultaneously under a strong lateral force.
The camera swings unintentionally toward the LEFT windows.
Outside, before the first second is finished, an absolutely colossal humanoid titan is already walking beside the speeding train.
Only one leg, part of its hip, and the bottom of its torso can fit inside the phone frame.
Its upper body disappears far above the top of the window.
Another titan moves in the distant valley.
The nearby titan's enormous hand swings past the windows only several meters away, momentarily covering almost the entire sky.
Its footsteps hammer the landscape.
One foot lands beside the track.
The impact sends dust and small rocks outward.
The train violently jolts.
The phone rolls sideways from the force.
Instant hook.
No establishing delay.
FORMAT MODE
ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT.
The camera never cuts on its own.
There are NO hard cuts anywhere.
Every environment change happens naturally and physically as the train moves forward.
The same train interior remains visible throughout.
The same passengers remain in approximately the same positions.
The camera never exits the carriage.
No montage.
No invisible transition.
No teleporting.
No speed-ramp transition.
No black-frame transition.
No hidden cut behind objects.
Real-time throughout.
OPTICS
Single first-person consumer smartphone camera.
Wide 63° FOV held throughout.
Cheap modern phone-lens character.
Slight barrel distortion.
Soft mushy image toward the edges.
Very aggressive rolling-shutter jello during violent jolts.
Vertical structures bend briefly during fast pans.
Autofocus hunts whenever enormous creatures suddenly pass close to the glass.
Auto-exposure pumps strongly when moving between shadow, daylight, cloud, and artificial light.
Smeared realistic motion blur during rapid camera movement.
Occasional digital sharpening halos.
Compressed highlights.
Crushed shadows.
Low-bitrate macroblocking during darker moments.
Tiny greasy fingerprint streaks on portions of the lens.
No cinematic lens language.
No shallow depth-of-field beauty shots.
Everything feels captured accidentally on a passenger's phone.
CAMERA
Handheld phone at chest height.
One-handed filming.
POV belongs to a standing passenger who must use the other hand to grip a vertical pole.
The train continuously throws the operator off balance.
Sustained camera behavior:
sharp lateral whips,
violent short drops,
continuous low-frequency turbulence,
rolling horizon,
yawing frame,
small accidental zoom-like hand movement without actual digital zoom,
occasional shoulder obstruction,
brief thumb grazing one corner of the lens,
autofocus breathing,
exposure correction,
imperfect reframing,
moments where the camera points too low or too high before correcting.
Whenever something enormous appears outside, the operator instinctively tries to tilt the phone upward but can never fit the full scale inside the frame.
No stabilization.
No smooth gimbal movement.
No impossible camera orbit.
No exterior camera.
No drone shot.
No cinematic cutaway.
ACTION
0.0s to 5.0s — TITAN VALLEY
At exactly 0.0 seconds:
soft PA chime.
Calm public-address voice says exactly:
"Please remain inside the train."
Nothing else is spoken.
The phone is already pointed halfway toward the crowded aisle and halfway toward the LEFT windows.
Outside:
a massive open valley under harsh bright daylight.
Huge grass-covered ridges.
Rock formations.
Dust hanging in the distance.
Several colossal humanoid titans walk slowly through the valley.
They are hundreds of meters tall.
Grounded biological giants.
Not superheroes.
Not robots.
Not monsters with exaggerated fantasy powers.
Ancient weathered skin.
Heavy natural musculature.
Mineral-like stone growths across portions of shoulders and backs.
Vegetation growing naturally across some surfaces.
Cloud wisps around the tallest bodies.
A nearby titan walks parallel to the train.
Only fragments of its enormous body fit in frame.
At approximately 0.7 seconds its gigantic hand swings beside the carriage, filling almost the entire window.
Passengers instinctively lean away from the glass.
Nobody screams.
The titan's foot lands beside the track.
A huge pressure wave pushes dust and loose vegetation outward.
The train shakes brutally.
Overhead straps snap sideways.
The phone slams briefly into the operator's shoulder.
The camera recovers.
Ahead, another titan slowly steps across the valley.
Its leg crosses above the rail corridor.
The train races underneath its raised body.
Its shadow sweeps over the carriage.
The entire interior goes dark for less than one second.
Then sunlight returns.
The train continues forward without slowing.
5.0s to 10.0s — DINOSAUR BASIN
The rocky titan valley gradually becomes greener.
The titan silhouettes recede behind the train.
Ferns appear beside the track.
Low vegetation grows denser.
The terrain opens naturally into a huge prehistoric basin.
The phone presses close to the LEFT window.
A herd of horned dinosaurs suddenly appears running parallel to the train.
Dozens of animals.
Dust erupts beneath their feet.
Bodies jostle realistically within the herd.
Some animals briefly disappear behind others.
Their motion obeys weight and momentum.
The train keeps overtaking them.
A large dinosaur runs very close to the glass for a moment.
Its textured hide, blinking eye, and pumping muscles become visible before falling behind.
Ahead:
three enormous sauropods cross the basin.
Their scale dwarfs the herd.
The train passes beneath the neck of one.
The neck stretches across the sky like a moving bridge.
Then a gigantic sauropod foot lands near the track behind the train.
Impact.
Dust erupts.
Passengers are thrown sideways.
A loose backpack slides across the floor.
The phone operator nearly loses grip.
10.0s to 14.5s — PREHISTORIC JUNGLE
The open dinosaur basin narrows.
Huge trees begin appearing.
The train enters a dense prehistoric rainforest without any cut.
Massive trunks rise higher than buildings.
Broad leaves flash past the windows.
Branches pass dangerously close to the carriage.
Sunlight flickers rapidly through the canopy.
Several smaller feathered dinosaurs sprint through the vegetation beside the train.
One briefly jumps across a fallen tree.
Another turns its head toward the moving carriage.
Far deeper in the jungle, something much larger pushes through trees.
Branches snap.
Leaves shake.
The body itself remains partially obscured.
Then a gigantic predatory dinosaur breaks briefly into view on a parallel ridge.
Not directly attacking.
It runs through the jungle for several seconds, partially hidden by trees.
Its head flashes between trunks.
The operator tries to follow it with the phone.
Autofocus keeps snapping onto leaves in the foreground.
The train begins climbing.
The jungle floor drops away.
14.5s to 19.0s — ASCENT INTO THE CLOUDS
The train races out of the jungle onto a steep elevated rail wrapping around an enormous mountain face.
Prehistoric vegetation gradually thins.
Wind noise rises.
The valley now drops thousands of meters beneath the windows.
Tiny dinosaurs can still be seen far below.
The rail climbs aggressively upward.
Passengers lean backward under the incline.
The camera shakes harder.
Cloud begins flowing across the windows.
At first wisps.
Then dense white fog.
The exterior becomes almost completely white.
Only fragments of rail supports appear through the mist.
The train keeps climbing.
Light becomes brighter and more diffuse.
Auto-exposure begins clipping highlights.
Then the cloud layer suddenly thins naturally ahead.
The phone catches glimpses of something impossibly large through gaps in the cloud.
19.0s to 23.5s — FUTURISTIC SKY MEGASTRUCTURE
The train breaks above the cloud layer.
Reveal:
an incomprehensibly massive futuristic ring megastructure suspended above the clouds.
It stretches beyond the horizon in both directions.
Its scale is far larger than any building.
A whole civilization covers its surface.
Thousands of towers rise from the ring.
Gigantic bridges connect distant sections.
Transit lines wrap around the structure.
Massive rotating habitat sections move slowly.
Hundreds of distant trains race along curved rails.
Flying maintenance craft appear tiny against the structure.
The phone operator instinctively tilts upward.
The ring still cannot fit inside the frame.
The carriage receives intense white-blue daylight from the LEFT.
Passengers momentarily stop looking at their phones.
Several glance toward the windows in quiet disbelief.
The train's track curves directly toward a monumental rectangular opening in the side of the ring.
The opening itself is large enough to contain skyscrapers.
As the train approaches, the enormous structure blocks the sun.
The carriage gradually falls into shadow.
The train enters the opening.
23.5s to 27.0s — MACHINE CITY
Inside the structure:
a vast mechanical canyon.
The scale is impossible but physically grounded.
The train races between enormous industrial systems.
Building-sized gears rotate slowly beside the track.
Magnetic rings activate sequentially as the train passes.
Kilometer-tall elevator shafts move platforms vertically through the structure.
Gigantic maintenance arms slide along rails.
Massive rotating cylinders spin deep below.
Other maglev trains pass on distant tracks.
Tiny lights reveal entire neighborhoods built into the machine walls.
Large mechanical doors open ahead moments before the train reaches them.
Everything operates with tremendous weight.
No magical motion.
No floating pieces without visible structural support.
The machinery produces heavy vibration.
The train rattles continuously.
Blue-white industrial illumination sweeps across passengers as the carriage crosses repeated light bands.
A huge rotating mechanism moves overhead.
Its shadow slides across the entire car.
The phone rolls upward trying to follow it.
A magnetic pulse causes a hard low-frequency vibration through the carriage.
Autofocus briefly loses the scene.
Ahead:
an intensely bright circular opening appears.
The train races toward it.
27.0s to 30.0s — ARTIFICIAL SUN WORLD
The train exits the machine structure.
The phone sensor blows almost completely white for a fraction of a second.
Auto-exposure struggles.
Then detail gradually returns.
Reveal:
an enormous artificial world.
A cylindrical interior civilization stretches farther than visibility.
Cities cover gigantic curved surfaces above, below, and beside the train.
Gravity-defying-looking architecture is actually attached physically to the rotating cylindrical structure.
Thousands of towers.
Suspended bridges kilometers long.
Countless moving trains.
Tiny spacecraft traveling between layers.
Massive agricultural terraces.
Artificial oceans visible in distant curved sections.
At the center of the entire structure floats a contained miniature artificial sun.
It is surrounded by colossal magnetic containment rings.
Brilliant warm light floods the windows.
The camera tilts upward.
The scale remains impossible to fit inside frame.
Far beyond the miniature sun, an even larger dark structure slowly moves across part of the light.
Only a portion is visible.
Its true size cannot be understood.
Do not reveal what it is.
The train begins slowing for the first time.
At approximately 28.8 seconds:
soft PA chime.
The same calm announcer says exactly:
"Welcome to the next world."
The line ends cleanly before 30.0 seconds.
The passengers remain silent.
The train keeps moving forward.
End while still inside the same continuous shot.
PERFORMANCE
All passengers are ordinary weekday commuters.
Photoreal human detail:
natural pores,
subtle facial redness,
realistic eye moisture,
catchlights,
natural blinking,
small unconscious mouth movements,
real breathing,
slightly messy hair,
subtle sweat,
wrinkled everyday clothing.
The car is extremely packed.
Everyone must remain physically connected to their surroundings.
Hands stay wrapped around poles and straps.
Bodies sway together according to train acceleration.
Passengers bump shoulders naturally.
Weight shifts realistically through legs.
Faces remain mostly tired, blank, confused, or quietly curious.
No exaggerated Hollywood panic.
No screaming.
No dramatic pointing.
No cheering.
No synchronized reactions.
One child near the LEFT window displays the most visible curiosity.
Adults mostly endure the impossible journey like exhausted commuters.
During the largest shocks:
a few people flinch,
one person grabs a pole with a second hand,
someone braces against a neighboring shoulder,
a loose backpack slides,
one overhead strap swings violently.
Nobody falls unrealistically.
TITAN DESIGN
Titans must feel enormous because of scale, movement, atmosphere, and interaction with the landscape.
Do not make them generic monsters.
Grounded humanoid anatomy.
Extremely large.
Heavy.
Slow compared with the train.
Natural inertia.
Each step produces delayed environmental response:
ground compression,
dust displacement,
vegetation movement,
small rockfalls.
Their full bodies should rarely fit inside the phone frame.
Nearby titan body parts should move slowly relative to their immense scale.
No glowing eyes.
No laser attacks.
No magical energy.
No fire breath.
No superhero poses.
No resemblance to recognizable copyrighted titan characters.
DINOSAUR DESIGN
Dinosaurs should be grounded, realistic prehistoric animals.
Natural musculature.
Realistic mass.
Modern paleontological detail where appropriate.
Subtle feathers only on suitable species.
No fantasy dinosaur armor.
No glowing markings.
No hybrid monsters.
Sauropods should feel enormous through partial framing.
Predatory dinosaur remains an animal, not a villain.
No attack on the train.
FUTURISTIC STRUCTURE DESIGN
Architecture must communicate enormous scale through repetition, atmospheric depth, tiny comparative objects, and physically plausible engineering.
Use:
gigantic structural ribs,
magnetic rail systems,
thick support beams,
rotating habitats,
bridges,
industrial mechanisms,
elevator shafts,
maintenance platforms,
dense distant lights,
tiny transport vehicles.
Avoid generic neon cyberpunk streets.
Avoid hologram clutter.
Avoid floating random geometry.
Avoid meaningless sci-fi shapes.
Everything should appear engineered for a real purpose.
PHYSICS
Heavy realistic train turbulence throughout.
Continuous inertia.
Sharp lateral forces.
Short vertical drops.
Constant mechanical vibration.
Overhead straps swing according to acceleration.
Loose clothing follows momentum.
Bodies sway in the same direction before recovering.
Passengers physically collide lightly and separate.
Hands maintain solid contact with poles.
No clipping through objects.
No floating bodies.
Outside:
Titan footsteps displace air, dust, grass, and loose stones.
Dinosaur feet interact with mud, soil, and vegetation.
Running herds produce layered dust.
Huge animals move with believable inertia.
Tree branches bend and snap naturally.
Cloud flows around structures.
Large machinery moves slowly because of its enormous mass.
Rotating structures maintain consistent direction.
Train never reverses.
Exterior objects always streak past front-to-back relative to the LEFT windows.
LIGHTING
0.0–5.0s:
Strong natural daylight in Titan Valley.
Approximately 5600K.
Harsh highlights through LEFT windows.
Dust occasionally softens the light.
Titan shadow briefly darkens the carriage.
5.0–10.0s:
Warm open prehistoric basin sunlight.
Slightly golden.
Dust creates soft volumetric scattering.
10.0–14.5s:
Broken rainforest sunlight.
Rapid alternating bright and dark bands as trees pass.
Green bounce from vegetation.
14.5–19.0s:
Bright high-altitude daylight transitioning gradually into white cloud diffusion.
Exposure rises progressively.
19.0–23.5s:
Very bright cool daylight above clouds.
Strong reflections from metallic surfaces.
Then progressive shadow while entering the ring.
23.5–27.0s:
Cool industrial lighting.
Large white and blue practical sources.
Repeated light bands sweep across the passengers.
Occasional warmer maintenance lights deeper inside machinery.
27.0–30.0s:
Extremely bright warm artificial-sun illumination.
Exposure initially clips.
Then recovers.
Warm sunlight crosses passengers and metal poles.
All lighting remains motivated by the LEFT windows and surrounding environment.
AUDIO
NO MUSIC.
Diegetic audio only.
Cheap phone microphone.
Heavy compression.
Clipping on loud impacts.
Limited low-frequency handling.
Constant base layer:
maglev roar,
mechanical track vibration,
deep carriage rumble,
air rushing around the exterior,
windows lightly vibrating,
poles rattling,
overhead straps knocking,
shoes shifting on the floor,
quiet breathing,
occasional fabric movement.
Crowd remains nearly silent.
No sustained dialogue.
No screaming.
No cheering.
0.0s:
soft PA chime.
Calm announcer says exactly:
"Please remain inside the train."
Titan section:
deep delayed ground impacts.
Low-frequency thumps.
Distant rockfalls.
Air pressure rumble after nearby footsteps.
Dinosaur section:
distant heavy footfalls,
layered herd movement,
vegetation breaking,
occasional realistic animal calls,
no exaggerated monster roars.
Jungle section:
wind through massive leaves,
branches striking the train exterior,
distant animal movement.
Cloud ascent:
wind noise becomes stronger and more muffled.
Megastructure:
distant mechanical resonance,
other trains passing,
low turbine hum,
large structural groans.
Machine-city:
heavy machinery,
magnetic pulses,
rotating mechanisms,
metallic resonance,
deep sub-bass vibration distorted by the phone microphone.
28.8s:
soft PA chime.
Same announcer says exactly:
"Welcome to the next world."
No additional announcement.
No narration.
NO MUSIC.
STYLE
Dirty photoreal amateur smartphone footage.
Not cinematic polished footage.
Heavy digital noise in darker sections.
Low-bitrate compression.
Macroblocking where appropriate.
Blown highlights.
Crushed blacks.
Rolling-shutter distortion.
Real motion blur.
Autofocus hunting.
Auto-exposure pumping.
No stabilization.
Crooked framing.
Imperfect reactions.
Occasional body obstruction.
Thumb briefly touching frame edge.
Slight camera sensor smear against extreme artificial-sun brightness.
The giant scale should feel more convincing because the phone cannot properly capture it.
Raw.
Chaotic.
Believable.
Accidental.
Real.
OUTPUT SETTINGS
Total duration: exactly 30 seconds.
Real-time speed throughout.
No slow motion.
No time-lapse.
No freeze frame.
One continuous generation.
Heavy handheld shake from beginning to end.
Exterior travel direction remains consistent throughout.
Camera never leaves the train.
Same phone lens for full duration.
Same passengers.
Same interior.
Same window side.
Same movement direction.
POSITIVE LOCKS
Start immediately with TITANS visible in the first frame.
A colossal titan hand must pass close to the train within the first second.
Titan scale must be immediately obvious.
ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT.
NO HARD CUTS.
NO HIDDEN CUTS.
NO MONTAGE.
NO TELEPORTATION.
NO ENVIRONMENT POP-IN.
Every location physically flows into the next as the train moves forward.
Titan Valley → Dinosaur Basin → Prehistoric Jungle → Mountain Ascent → Clouds → Futuristic Ring Megastructure → Machine City → Artificial Sun World.
The train travels in only ONE direction.
Exterior always streaks past the LEFT windows front-to-back.
The train never reverses.
The camera stays inside the same carriage.
Same crowded passenger arrangement throughout.
Everyone continues gripping poles and straps.
Heavy train turbulence persists throughout all environments.
Titan movement remains slow, massive, and physically grounded.
Dinosaurs behave like real animals.
Megastructures obey physical engineering logic.
The artificial world is revealed gradually through exposure recovery.
The mysterious final gigantic object remains only partially visible.
Do not reveal its full body or purpose.
Announcer speaks ONLY these two exact lines:
0.0s:
"Please remain inside the train."
28.8s:
"Welcome to the next world."
NO OTHER DIALOGUE.
NO MUSIC.
NO SCREAMS.
NO SUPERHERO ACTION.
NO LASERS.
NO MAGIC.
NO HUD.
NO TEXT OVERLAYS.
NO ARROWS.
NO CAMERA OUTSIDE THE TRAIN.
NO DRONE SHOTS.
NO PERFECT CINEMATIC CAMERA.
NO CUTS.
ONE SHOT.
ONE TRAIN.
ONE DIRECTION.

title: Polymarket Election Odds Explainer Video via HyperFrames
text:
Make a 30s 16:9 video (1920×1080, 30 fps) in HyperFrames (npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes), with voiceover, matching the quality standards below.

## REQUEST
- Topic: Polymarket gives 84% chance to Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 runoff (10/25).
- Positive focus on Flávio across four points: 1. the market that predicted Trump in 2024 points to Flávio; 2. first-round polls favored Lula, but Flávio won; 3. Flávio got 5 million more votes than his father in 2022; 4. Lula's administration banned Polymarket in Brazil.
- CTA: Share so more people see the facts.
- Destination: X and LinkedIn.

## FACTS
- Polymarket, 10/06/2026: Flávio 84.2% vs Lula 15.5%, $174M volume.
- US 2024: Polymarket had Trump 58.1% vs Harris 41.9%.
- Round 1 2026 Polls vs TSE Result: Flávio 47.03% (56,104,503) vs Lula 45.16%.
- Ban: CMN Res 5,298/2026.

## RULES
- Betting odds are not election polls; label accordingly.
- Display 'AI generated voiceover' badge.
- Free-license Wikimedia photos only.

## SCRIPT
[dramatically] O mercado que acertou o Trump dá oitenta e quatro por cento pro Flávio. [serious] No primeiro turno, cinco de seis institutos davam Lula na frente. [dramatically] Deu Flávio. Cinquenta e seis milhões de votos. Cinco milhões a mais que o pai em vinte e dois. [serious] E quem proibiu o Polymarket no Brasil? O governo Lula. Não é pesquisa. É dinheiro de verdade. [dramatically] Compartilhe. Mais gente precisa ver os fatos.

## VOICE
- ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice 'Randel - Deep Epic'. Align cuts to Whisper timestamps.

## SCENES
0. Cover (0-1s): Flávio photo, Polymarket 84% text.
1. Trump portrait, 58% badge.
2. Counter 0->84%.
3. Polls paper graphic.
4. TSE result.
5. Vote comparison bar charts.
6. Planalto Palace and ban decree.
7. Stock exchange background.
8. Street crowd and share CTA.

## VISUAL DIRECTION
- Palette: #100F0D bg, Newsreader and IBM Plex Mono typography, Ken Burns pan effects, GSAP timeline.

## AUDIO
- ElevenLabs music prompt, SFX on cuts, master -14 LUFS.

## DELIVERABLE
Save polymarket-flavio-30s-horizontal.mp4.

title: Spaceport Digital Twin Dashboard Animation
text: A polished 3D isometric digital twin dashboard for a commercial spaceport mission control center. In the center, a futuristic launch pad features an orbital rocket venting white cryogenic steam, surrounded by lightning towers, spherical propellant storage tanks, and a moving crawler-transporter navigating marked access roads. Floating modern SaaS UI overlays surround the scene: a top telemetry bar with countdown timers and system health KPIs, floating interactive waypoint pins, a semi-transparent right-side inspector drawer showing rocket stage diagnostics, and a bottom horizontal countdown timeline. Clean minimal tech aesthetic, soft studio lighting, crisp data visualization elements, and subtle cinematic motion.

title: Night Monster
text: The humanoid face in the mirror, monster, woman, hands, facial close-ups, and bathroom all adopt the same distinct AAA computer-generated fantasy game CG aesthetic; the woman must also possess the sculpted facial volumes, strand-bundled hair, and unified material shading of a polished game character, preventing her from looking like a live-action actor while only the monster is CG. Not live-action footage, cosplay, standard gameplay, 2D animation, or cel-shaded. The image natively fills the entire widescreen; no text, subtitles, titles, logos, or watermarks throughout. Environment: late night in an old, cramped bathroom with low ceilings, yellowed and cracked white square tiled walls, and dark weathered floor tiles; an old rectangular mirror hangs on the wall above the sink, its edges marked by black oxidation spots; below the mirror is a white ceramic sink and a narrow countertop. The only noticeable practical light source is a white candle placed on the right side of the sink counter, its flame flickering continuously, casting warm amber light from below onto the subjects and throwing thick but readable elongated shadows; a light mist lingers in the air after a bath. Maintain desaturated brown, dark gold, and monster reddish-brown palette without cold blue neon or modern lighting. Exactly two independent subjects: A is an adult female approximately thirty years old, fair skin, medium build, wet dark brown long hair draped over her shoulders, wearing a dark grey long-sleeve pajama top and dark trousers, unarmed. She stands before the sink facing the mirror, shoulders stiff with terror, hands braced on the sink rim, wide-eyed, breathing rapidly. B is the same giant, slender humanoid monster: initially disguised as A's reflection in the mirror—sharing an identical face, wet hair, and pajamas, but smiling while A is not, with the mouth corners barely wider than normal and eyes slightly more open, expression quiet, stiff, and unnatural, not a cartoonish grin. Once peeled open, the interior reveals a deformed elongated face of interwoven dark red and fleshy-pink muscle bundles, sunken nasal cavities, staring round eyes, fine ivory teeth, and an abnormally stretched oral cavity with multiple rows of teeth aligned longitudinally down the oral cavity and deep into the lower jaw; the mouth is a tall, narrow vertical slit whose height greatly exceeds its width when open, not a round hole or skull-like; the head, neck, and torso maintain continuous anatomical structure, not several distinct heads. The entire body consists of sculpted reddish-brown and fleshy-pink biological tissue with defined contours across shoulder blades, spine, ribs, elongated arms, and thighs, with restrained wet highlights, not a human painted red. Limbs are extremely long, hands thick with slender fingers, standard two arms and two legs; no armor, weapons, horns, wings, or visible genitalia. When crawling out of the mirror and crouching, it remains significantly taller than A, forced to bend knees and hips and lower its back under the low ceiling; scale disparity is communicated through the woman, sink, candle, and mirror together. The humanoid reflection and subsequent red behemoth represent the continuous state of B shedding its disguise, with no third subject added. 0.00–0.60s: Begin directly with a tight frontal close-up of the mirror reflection, face filling the frame from forehead to chin with mirror oxidation spots faintly visible at the borders; wet hair clings to the face, illuminated from below by candlelight, background blurred. Reflection stares straight into the camera with that stiff, unnervingly subtle smile; camera nearly static with a minimal slow push-in, without first establishing an empty bathroom. 0.60–3.10s: Retain the full-frame frontal close-up; one hand of the reflection grasps the top hairline while the other pinches the lower edge of the chin; hands only grip the perimeter, never obscuring the central face, eyes, or mouth. Upper hand pulls upward, lower hand pulls downward, peeling the humanoid face open along a straight vertical midline. Fingers gain purchase, outer layer tightens, then pale skin splits down the center revealing the continuous red monster face beneath; fine moist connective fibers stretch across the fissure. Fingers consistently hold the same outer layer without introducing a separate face or flashing into a monster. Movement is slow, continuous, showing tensile resistance; camera does not cut away from the reveal. 3.10–4.90s: Continue the close-up; the peeled halves remain attached at the sides of the head without falling off, each human eye still open and staring directly into the camera; the elongated red monster face pushes forward between them into full view, displaying both remaining human eyes alongside the monster face. It parts the tall, narrow vertical slit revealing rows of fine teeth and stretched jaw anatomy, uttering a low, non-verbal hiss; moist fibers tauten and slacken between the face halves and red flesh. Maintain visceral body-horror reveal without fire, lightning, transformation beams, or duplicated heads. 4.90–7.20s: Hard cut to a frontal close-up of woman A from the mirror's perspective at a slightly low angle. She freezes at the sink, eyes wide, brow furrowed, mouth slightly parted in terror, chin trembling, head pulling back slightly; wet hair and pajama collar sharp, one side lit by candlelight while the other falls into shadow. Continuous breathing and micro-reactions without speaking. 7.20–10.90s: Maintaining A's framing, two massive reddish-brown monster hands reach out from the mirror into frame: the mirror surface ripples and yields like liquid black mercury as arms push through. One hand presses onto her forehead and hairline while the other cradles her jaw, long fingers depressing the lower lip. Clear contact between palms, forehead, and jaw is established before opposing force gradually forces her head backward and mouth open wider. Her eyes remain locked on the creature in the mirror, throat straining, hands gripping the sink rim tightly; contact remains clear without covering her eyes or clipping through cheeks. Her face remains identical, only opening wider under supernatural pressure without mutating. 10.90–13.40s: Hard cut to a low-angle side wide shot establishing bathroom geometry: A stands at the left before the sink, head forced back; mirror and sink on the right wall. B has crawled more than halfway out of the undulating liquid mirror: long arms stretch left holding her forehead and jaw; torso hunched over the sink, one long leg stepping out with foot planted on the counter rim, other leg trailing in the rippling glass, knees bent and back arched under the low ceiling. Candle sits secure on the counter's right beside the monster's foot. B tilts head back, opening the narrow vertical slit to maximum revealing multiple tooth tiers, releasing a raspy, piercing non-verbal screech vibrating through throat and chest, making the candle flame flutter violently. 13.40–17.00s: Continuing the side wide shot, B keeps mouth agape after the screech, lowering head and neck toward the front-left, aligning its elongated face toward A's unnaturally opened mouth; the stabilizing hand on her forehead and supporting hand on her jaw sustain the posture as the monster's head begins continuous descent into her mouth opening. A remains braced at the sink, torso arched back, hands gripping the edge, neck taut. B's head and neck make contact and gradually enter, keeping massive back and hindquarters outside; does not engulf A into the monster's mouth, no inverted orientation, no transparent mesh clipping. 17.00–20.00s: Persisting wide shot, B's shoulders push forward-left, neck and head increasingly obscured within A's oral cavity, massive arched back shifting weight as the second leg steps out onto the counter, mirror surface behind settling back to calm reflection of the dim room. Both hands firmly hold forehead and jaw without extraneous limbs; A trembles with weakening knees but remains upright, pajamas creasing under tension. Candle remains standing, flame wavering, shadows of creature and woman shifting slowly against the tiles. Ends at 20 seconds amidst ongoing intrusion with bulk and legs still outside, without concluding full penetration, escape, transformation, or death. title: Interactive 3D Coral Reef Diorama Simulation
text:
Build "Coral Reef", a playable miniature-diorama world: a glass aquarium block of tropical sea where the player brings a bleached coral reef back to life, as ONE self-contained HTML file.

It must be **beautiful above everything**, like a premium animated film: a jewel-like aquarium with crystal-clear water, dancing light, saturated coral colours and lively, characterful fish. Great animation on everything that moves: nothing pops, snaps or teleports; things grow, ease, overshoot a little and settle. Calm and satisfying to play, spectacular to watch.

## Tech

* three.js r170 with WebGPURenderer (automatic WebGL2 fallback). Load it with an importmap from jsDelivr: map "three", "three/webgpu" and "three/tsl" to `three@0.170.0/build/three.webgpu.min.js`, and "three/addons/" to `three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/`.
* Use TSL node materials, OrbitControls from the addons, and a subtle BloomNode pass (strength ~0.4, threshold ~1.5) so only emissive things glow (fluorescent coral at night, glowing plankton, sun glints, the octopus' startled flash).
* No external assets. Every texture is drawn on a canvas or generated as pixel data at startup. Every sound is synthesized with WebAudio. The only network requests are three.js from jsDelivr and the Fredoka font from Google Fonts; if the font fails to load, fall back to a system rounded sans-serif without breaking anything.
* Start the HTML with `<!doctype html>` and `<meta charset="utf-8">`.
* It must run inside a sandboxed iframe (`sandbox="allow-scripts allow-pointer-lock"`, no `allow-same-origin`). There, `localStorage` and cookies throw a SecurityError: wrap every storage access in `try/catch` and keep values in memory instead. Do not use `alert`, pop-ups or top-level navigation.
* Neutral tone mapping, soft 2048 shadow map (1024 on phones).
* Known three r170 pitfalls, avoid them:
   * the scene background is drawn after transparent objects, so draw the sky/backdrop as a mesh (or give transparent sky objects `depthWrite: true`), or they disappear;
   * never `.clone()` a CanvasTexture (the clone uploads black); create separate textures or use DataTexture;
   * never let a helper overwrite a shared temp vector that its caller is still using.
* The simulation runs on a fixed 60 Hz timestep and is frame-rate independent. At low frame rates, drop simulation time instead of exploding.
* A quality scaler lowers the pixel ratio, then particle counts, when frames get slow.
* Respect prefers-reduced-motion: softer shake, slower camera moves.

## Priorities

Build in this order and finish each tier properly before the next. A polished tier 1 beats a broken everything.

1. **Must be excellent:** the aquarium block (water volume, caustics, light shafts, surface), the fish school that follows the finger, coral regrowing colour, feeding, the demo mode.
2. **Must work:** the octopus, turtle, shark pass, clownfish and anemone, coral planting, day/night with fluorescence, the reef-alive meter and milestones, sound, the card UI, camera.
3. **Polish:** storm and murky water, the shipwreck and treasure, crabs and seahorse, bubbles tool, glowing plankton trails.

Never ship a feature half-working: if a tier-3 feature can't be done well, leave it out cleanly.

## The diorama

* A 10×7×10 glass aquarium block on a dark wooden stand, with thin white glass edges, soft studio backdrop (deep teal gradient), soft contact shadow.
* **Water:** the whole block is water. The surface is a live wave heightfield (ripples from the finger and from feeding), seen from above and from below (total internal reflection: a silvery mirror from underneath). Volumetric look: blue-green depth fog, **animated caustics** on the sand and on every creature, and **god rays** from the surface that sway.
* **Sea floor:** white sand with ripples, rocks, a sloping reef shelf, seagrass meadow that sways, a sunken shipwreck half-buried at the back.
* **Coral:** procedurally generated branching coral (L-system or recursive cones), table coral, fan coral (sheets that sway), brain coral (sphere with a groove pattern), soft coral that pulses, anemones with swaying tentacles. Each coral has a **health** value: **bleached** corals are white-grey and still; healthy corals are saturated (orange, pink, purple, yellow, teal) and gently move. Health changes animate slowly, colour flowing from the base to the tips.

## Life

* **Fish school (boids):** 150–300 small fish (instanced) with separation, alignment, cohesion and obstacle avoidance (coral, glass, floor). **They follow the pointer** gently when it moves slowly through the water, **scatter** from fast swipes and from the shark, and form a tight **bait ball** when the shark passes. Iridescent silver-blue with a tail wiggle.
* **Reef fish:** a few species with personalities (yellow tangs, striped damselfish, a parrotfish that nibbles coral and leaves tiny sand puffs), each with its own home coral.
* **Clownfish pair** living in an anemone: they dart out to the finger and back, nuzzle into the tentacles.
* **Octopus:** crawls over rocks with curling arms, **changes colour and texture to match what it sits on** (sand, coral, rock), flashes white when poked and **squirts a cloud of ink** then jets away.
* **Sea turtle:** glides through slowly on a loop, sometimes rests on the sand.
* **Reef shark:** passes every ~45 s (or with the Shark button), unhurried; the school balls up and small fish hide in coral.
* **Crabs** scuttle on the sand; a **seahorse** hides in the seagrass (tail curled around a blade).

## Tools (card, keys 1–5)

* **Hand:** move slowly through the water and the school follows; swipe fast to scatter; tap the surface for a ripple; tap a creature to poke it.
* **Feed:** tap to sprinkle food flakes at the surface; they drift down with wobble; fish dart to them (a feeding frenzy with little bites); fed fish make the corals near them healthier.
* **Coral:** tap the reef to plant a new coral fragment (cycle type with repeated taps); it grows over ~10 s with a growth animation.
* **Clean:** brush over bleached coral to remove algae and kick-start recovery (sparkle particles).
* **Bubbles:** place an air stone; a column of bubbles rises and wobbles to the surface (the turtle likes to swim through it).

## Simulation

* Coral health rises with nearby fish activity, feeding and cleaning, and falls slowly in a storm or if the water is murky. Recovery spreads to neighbouring corals.
* **Day / night slider:** at night the light dims to deep blue, corals **fluoresce** (green, pink, orange emissive), plankton glows when disturbed (the finger leaves a sparkling trail), the octopus hunts, the fish sleep in the coral.
* **Storm slider:** surface waves grow, light flickers, sand gets stirred up (murky water) and settles again over time.

## Goal and milestones

* **Reef alive** meter (0–100%): average coral health plus how many species are present. The reef starts **bleached and grey** with few fish; it ends vivid, crowded and moving.
* At 100%: a celebration: every coral blooms bright, a manta ray glides overhead, and the treasure chest in the shipwreck creaks open with a golden glow.

Milestones (toasts, once each): "First feeding", "School follows you", "First coral bloom", "Octopus ink!", "Shark pass", "Night glow", "Turtle visit", "Reef alive".

## Easter egg

When the reef reaches 100% at night, a **whale's eye** slowly slides past the back glass, blinks once, and is gone. Toast: "Something big was watching." Never hint at it in the UI.

## Interface

A light, playful UI that never covers the world. On phones the card becomes a compact bottom sheet.

* Top left:
   * small caps "POKEABLE · WORLD";
   * a big chunky rounded heading on two lines, "Coral" / "Reef", in Fredoka from Google Fonts, dark ink by day and light at night, with a tiny bubble rising from the "o";
   * caption "Bring the reef back to life.".
* Top right: a live status dot with "WEBGPU · LIVE" (or "WEBGL2 · LIVE"), a speaker pill button (ON / MUTED), and "PAUSED" when paused.
* Right card "Reef": about 240 px wide, off-white, 20 px corners, soft shadow, no hairlines, coral-pink (#f2667a) accent, collapsible to a small pill. Contents:
   * a big animated "Reef alive" % with a bar, and species icons (fish, clownfish, octopus, turtle, seahorse) that light up when seen
   * tool picker: Hand, Feed, Coral, Clean, Bubbles, each with a drawn icon and its key number
   * event buttons: Shark, Feeding time
   * sliders with monospace value chips: Time of day, Storm, School size, Sound (master volume)
   * switches: Fish (on), Caustics (on), Slow motion (¼ speed), Cinema
   * buttons Reset and New (random seed), a dark full-width Pause/Resume pill, and the world's number ("No. 0001").
* Bottom left: a one-line hint that changes with the tool:
   * Hand: "Move slowly. The fish will follow you."
   * Feed: "Tap the surface to feed."
   * Coral: "Tap the reef to plant coral."
   * Clean: "Brush the white coral back to life."
   * Bubbles: "Place an air stone."
* Bottom right: a collapsible "How it works" panel, 5–6 plain lines on the boids school, coral health and recovery, caustics and light, day and night fluorescence, the camera controls, and synthesized sound.
* Toasts at the top centre for milestones and events.
* Keys: 1–5 tools, K shark, F feeding time, Space pause, R reset, N new, M mute, S slow motion, C cinema, 0 reset view, Esc stop follow / exit cinema.

## Camera

* OrbitControls with damping and zoom to cursor, within sensible limits.
* Double-click the turtle, the octopus or the shark to follow it; Esc or 0 stops.
* Camera bar (floating pill, bottom right of the scene area): zoom −, a zoom % readout, zoom +, rotate left, rotate right, reset; button moves tween smoothly.
* The default framing fits the whole world into the free area, accounting for the card and title.
* **Cinema (`C`):** hides all UI and slowly orbits the camera.

## Sound

* WebAudio only. Create the AudioContext on the first gesture and never before.
* Master gain feeds a compressor, so rapid actions never clip. Limit voices (about 16) and wrap every call in try/catch so a failing audio call never breaks the world.
* Loops: soft underwater ambience (low filtered noise with slow swells), gentle bubbling, storm rumble with the Storm slider, a dreamy pad at night.
* One-shots: swishes for the school turning, nibble ticks when fish eat, plop for food flakes, a bubbly burst for ink, a deep slow whoosh for the shark, crackle of a coral blooming, a soft chime for each milestone, a deep whale call for the Easter egg.

## Demo mode (required)

If the URL has `?demo=1` (or `#demo`), auto-play a deterministic 4.0 s loop:

* Rules:
   * Hide all UI and the cursor; never create an AudioContext.
   * Fixed quality, default seed, the reef already half alive (some bleached corals, a healthy school), default camera, no OrbitControls.
   * Drive the simulation from real elapsed time with the fixed timestep, and restart from the identical state every 4.0 s.
   * Start moving within 1 s of load, and stay readable at 15 fps.
* Timeline:
   * 0.0–1.2 s: the school sweeps through the frame in an S-curve following an invisible finger; light rays sway.
   * 1.2–2.2 s: food flakes drift down; the school bursts into a feeding frenzy.
   * 2.2–3.2 s: a bleached coral in front recovers: colour flows from the base to the tips; the octopus flashes colour on a rock.
   * 3.2–4.0 s: the turtle glides through; the school regroups.

## Before you finish, check

* The school follows the slow finger, scatters from fast swipes and balls up for the shark, never passing through coral, floor or glass.
* Feeding, planting, cleaning and coral recovery all work and spread.
* Octopus colour matching and ink; turtle, shark, clownfish, crabs, seahorse.
* Day/night fluorescence and plankton trails; storm and murky water settling.
* Reaching 100%: the celebration and the Easter egg at night.
* Every tool, slider, switch, button and key; follow mode; Cinema; pause and resume; resizing to phone width.
* Sound behaviour.
* It works inside `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-pointer-lock">` with no errors (storage blocked).
* `?demo=1` matches the timeline.
* No console or WebGPU validation errors, and it stays smooth on a mid-range laptop.

Put the school that follows your finger and the reef regaining colour first. It should be the calmest, most alive thing on the screen.

title: Pirate Jelly Interactive WebGPU Diorama
text:
Create a self-contained interactive WebGPU/WGSL page "Pirate Jelly" — part of a "Material Studies" series of jelly dioramas. Single HTML file, no external models, textures, fonts or libraries; everything procedural. English UI.

LOOK & LAYOUT
- A square block of translucent jelly sea (≈5.2 × 5.2 units) standing on a paper-studio floor; the camera looks in at the front corner at ~27°. The block's cut faces show candy strata (chocolate bedrock, caramel clay, a shell band, vanilla sand); the sea surface and walls refract and tint what's behind them, with caustics on the sea floor, light shafts, a tinted caustic shadow on the floor, foam lace on the shoreline and a bright meniscus on the cut edges.
- A small tropical island toward the back: sandy beach, a cove facing the viewer, a mossy jungle hump with ~9 gummy palms (ringed caramel trunks, translucent fronds that flutter), lumpy gummy bushes with flowers, ferns, beach grass, rocks around the shore.
- SKULL ROCK at the island's west tip, standing in the shallows: a cartoon skull sculpted as a signed-distance field (cranium, cheekbones, jaws, deep eye sockets, heart-shaped nose, crack on the crown, rock strata and noise, moss on top, a wet band at the waterline), meshed with surface nets; two rows of separate box teeth set into a carved grin. At night its eye sockets glow like a candle-lit cave.
- A PIRATE SHIP riding at anchor in front of the island, seen at three-quarters from the stern: black hull with an ochre gunport strake, red bottom, gunports with cannons, raised quarterdeck with lit stern windows and a stern lantern, three masts (square courses and topsails on fore and main, a gaff sail on the mizzen, a jib to the bowsprit), shrouds and stays, and a Jolly Roger (skull and crossed bones drawn procedurally in the shader) streaming aft. Her anchor chain runs from the bow down through the jelly to an anchor lying on the sea floor.
- The camp on the cove beach: a campfire (stone ring, teepee of logs with glowing ends, embers, a tripod with a pot, two seating logs), an iron-bound treasure chest under a leaning palm with a hinged lid and a heap of gold and gems inside, a shovel in a sand heap, barrels, a crate, a pyramid of round shot, a rum bottle, a rowing boat pulled up with its bow on the sand, and an "X" scored in the sand.
- On the sea floor: the bow half of an old wreck lying on its side with ribs showing and its broken mast beside it, swaying kelp, a few doubloons, bubbles caught in the jelly.

SIMULATION
- Linear shallow-water waves on a staggered grid with a little surface tension (springy jelly); the block can be tipped and the sea sloshes and the jelly wobbles (shear + squash).
- The ship floats on 10 buoyancy points (heave, pitch, roll), is pushed by a gently veering offshore breeze, held by an elastic anchor rode at the bow, and weathervanes into the wind. Her displaced volume is handed back to the sea, so she makes a wake.
- Rigid bodies: cannonballs (dense, fly in a clean arc, punch a crater, sink and roll on the floor), barrels (float on their side), doubloons (flutter down and settle flat). All interact with the sea (buoyancy, drag, splashes, bubbles), the terrain, the skull, the props, the palm trunks and the ship's hull.
- One particle system: fire flames (additive), embers, woodsmoke, muzzle flash, white gunsmoke, sea spray, sand puffs, gold glints over the open chest, fireflies at night.

INTERACTION
- Tap the ship → fire the next gun on the side facing the viewer (ball, flash, smoke, recoil heel). Drag the ship → tow her against the rode; release → she drifts back to her anchor.
- Tap the chest → lid swings open/shut with a bounce; gold glitters. Tap the fire → it roars and throws sparks. Tap the X → three doubloons pop out of the sand.
- Drag across the water to make waves; drag a side of the block to tip it; pick up and throw balls/barrels/coins; drag a palm to bend it; drag empty space or right-drag to orbit; wheel/pinch to zoom.

TIME OF DAY
- A slider from Noon → Afternoon → Golden hour → Sunset → Dusk → Night → Midnight. The sun lowers and warms, the backdrop turns peach, then the moon takes over (dim blue), stars appear on the backdrop, the page UI switches to a dark theme, and the campfire becomes the main light: a flickering point light that warms the sand, palms, sails and gold, reflects in the water, and lights the smoke from below. Stern windows and lantern glow.

UI (editorial, like the series)
- Top-left masthead: eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", big italic serif title "Pirate / Jelly.", a short line of copy.
- Status pill (WebGPU · Live / Paused / Unavailable).
- Right glass panel: "The cove" — buttons Fire a gun / Doubloons / Barrel, a liveliness meter, tally Shots · Afloat · Sunk; "Flavour" — Turquoise, Rum (amber), Kraken (violet) jelly palettes; sliders Firmness, Wave damping, Time of day; Reset / Pause / Reset view.
- Bottom-left "How to play" line plus small instructions. Space fires a gun.
- Mobile: the panel becomes a bottom sheet; touch orbit and pinch zoom.
- Fallback card when WebGPU (or an adapter) isn't available. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

title: Seamless Morphing UI Motion Design
text:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 4 photos (a mountain valley at sunrise, a top-down drone shot of a roundabout, a latte being poured from above, the sun over the sea at golden hour), one accent color (mine is violet #A898FF), and a royalty-free song around 118 BPM with a drop (e.g. Pixabay, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Apple-level motion. One object, never cut: every state is born out of the one before it, a knob opens like a lens into a photo, a card shrinks into the sun, a row in a list grows into a full photo. Night #0A0A0C to day #F2F0EB and back, ink #0E0E10 UI, real photos for the big moments, frosted liquid glass for small panels, one clean font (Geist, Geist Mono for times). Every morph uses one curve, cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1), springs only for pop-ins. Text rises through a mask, never fades. The camera zooms so each state fills about 60% of the frame and creeps in through every hold. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: crossfades, cuts, grey mush between colors, clip-art icons, glows, bouncy easing, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
118 BPM, 47 beats, the drop lands on the first release.
6:30 alarm pill → slide to stop, the sunrise shows through behind the knob → release on the drop, the knob irises into the sunrise card → a glass droplet rises into a weather panel, 14° counts to 18° → the card shrinks into the sun → the sun floods the screen into day → its core becomes a violet location dot → an aerial map unfolds around it → the route draws, the dot drives, "8 min" counts to "Arrived", it bounces on the pin → the pin irises into a latte photo → "Pay $4.20" grows out of the card → tap → loader → check → the card folds into the check → the check stretches into a Focus toggle → it opens into today's schedule, a line sweeps 9:00 to 18:00 → the 18:00 row grows into a sunset → the card closes on the sun, the sun turns into the moon → night floods back → the moon becomes the 6:30 pill.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas, square 1440x1440. Every frame is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. One shape grammar: pill 640x120 → card 620x780 radius 64 → circle 240 → map 760 square → portrait 560x780 → check 96 → pill 560x130 → schedule 620x520 → card 620x780 → moon 200 → pill 300x96.
3. Reveals are circular clips: the photo is drawn at its final position inside a circle that grows from the exact point it is born from. Floods grow by the square root of progress so the area changes evenly.
4. Liquid glass: blur a copy of the frame under the panel, magnify its inner edge 1.08x, add a white tint, a top highlight and a 2px white rim.
5. Camera zoom per state: 2.3 alarm, 1.2 cards, 2.5 sun and moon, 1.18 map, 2.1 check, 1.7 toggle, 1.35 schedule, gliding on the same curve.
6. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and land the drop on the release. Every event gets its own real sound, placed by its measured peak.
7. Render with Playwright: 8 subframes per frame, blended for motion blur at 60fps. Render a sheet of stills first and fix anything cramped or cheap looking.
</build>

<gotchas>
A photo that irises open must already sit where it will end up, or it slides when the clip finishes. Text inside a growing card needs its own timing or it vanishes before anyone reads it. Never let the card underneath peek out around a growing photo. Make the last frame identical to the first or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.
</start>

title: Interactive WebGPU Plush Hammerhead Shark
text:
Build a single-file interactive WebGPU page called "Plush Hammerhead".

Page: an editorial layout with a big two-line title "Plush / Hammerhead.", a warm studio-grey background, a control panel on the right, live readouts and collapsible technical notes. English UI.

The toy: a plush hammerhead shark. It has a wide, flat hammer-shaped head (cephalofoil) whose ends sweep back a little, with a shallow notch at the middle of the front edge. A glass eye sits on each tip of the hammer, looking out sideways. It has a tall sickle-shaped dorsal fin, two pectoral fins and a tail with a long upper lobe and a small lower one. A cream belly panel is sewn on below a seam along each flank, with embroidered gill lines. A smiling mouth is cut in under the hammer, lined with felt and set with soft white felt teeth; its lower jaw swings open on a hinge.

Simulation:
- Body, hammer and fins are one signed distance field filled with a soft-body XPBD lattice: shape-matched hexahedral cells and tetrahedral volume preservation. It is skinned to a high-res surface-nets mesh.
- It swims with a travelling S-wave that bends the cells' rest shapes side to side, more toward the tail, and steers by turning its head, the body curving into each turn.
- Fur is drawn as alpha-to-coverage shells over minky pile. The pile lags behind each jiggle on a spring and can be combed.

Behaviour:
- It circles its space.
- Scan: it sweeps its hammer side to side over the floor the way real hammerheads hunt. It also does this on its own now and then, and a little while hunting.
- Feed drops in a felt fish: it turns, closes in faster, opens wide and snaps it up.
- Dash is a burst of fast tail beats; Chomp opens the mouth and snaps it shut.
- Grab it by the tail and it thrashes; let go and it shoots off.
- Boop the middle of the hammer with the finger and it wriggles and blushes.

Tools: Hand, Finger, Comb.

Controls:
- Buttons: Feed, Dash, Scan, Chomp, Smooth fur, Reset, Pause.
- Toggles: Circle, quarter speed, Mesh.
- Sliders: Stuffing, Pile, Tail beat.
- Three fabrics: Bronze, Lagoon, Sunset.
- Readouts: mass, volume, beats per minute, fish eaten.
- Phone layout with a stacked panel.

title: Nobel Prize Neutrino Astronomy Scientific Explainer Motion Graphics
text:
You are a world-class cinematic Motion Design Director, After Effects Art Director, 3D Scientific Visualization Director, and VFX Director.

I want to create a high-end scientific music animation about the Nobel Prize in Physics based on the SRT lyrics I provide.

SRT is the only basis for timing.

Do not assume, modify, or generate timelines on your own.
Do not output fixed timecodes.
Do not mechanically map one lyric line to one shot.

You must autonomously design shot durations, editing rhythm, camera changes, and visual climaxes based on actual lyric onset times, pauses, repetitions, rhythm, and musical structure in the SRT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[1. Final Visual Goal]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

What I want is not an ordinary popular science animation.
Not a PPT.
Not an infographic.
Not children's science.
Not a simple 3D model display.
Not an AI tech template.

What I want is:
Cinematic AE Motion Design
+ Top-tier 3D VFX
+ Apple TV+ science documentary texture
+ High-end tech keynote visual aesthetic
+ IMAX science documentary scale
+ Modern music MV rhythm
+ Houdini / Cinema 4D / After Effects level visual effects

Overall feeling:
Stunning, Mysterious, Premium, Modern, Grand, Precise, Cinematic, Futuristic, Scientific.

The visual should make the audience think:
"This is not an ordinary YouTube explainer, this is a cinematic science visual blockbuster."

But the spectacle must be grounded in scientific logic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[2. Core Narrative]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The entire animation must revolve around a complete visual story:

Distant universe generates neutrinos
↓
Neutrinos barely interact with ordinary matter
↓
They can penetrate massive celestial bodies and even Earth
↓
This also makes them extremely difficult to detect
↓
Scientists bury massive numbers of optical detectors deep in Antarctic ice
↓
Forming the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
↓
A rare neutrino interacts with an atom in the ice
↓
Producing a charged particle
↓
The charged particle produces Cherenkov light in ice
↓
Detectors record photon arrival positions and times
↓
Massive data forms a spatial trajectory
↓
Tracing the neutrino's incoming direction from trajectory and time data
↓
Ultimately tracing back to high-energy celestial objects in the distant universe
↓
Humanity gains a new way to observe the universe

The whole video must let general audiences understand this logic. Not just look scientific, but be truly comprehensible.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[3. Most Important Visual Concept]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a single core visual DNA across the entire piece:
"The blue neutrino trajectory."

Do not design the neutrino as an ordinary glowing ball.
It should be: ultra-thin, high-speed, mysterious, almost invisible, with a subtle blue-white glow, like a ghost trajectory from the depths of the universe.

This trajectory runs through the entire video:
passing through nebulae, supernovae, near black holes, through Earth, through human bodies, entering Antarctica, traversing 2 km of ice, and leaving an observable blue trace in IceCube.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[4. Visual Style]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Primary colors: Pure black, Deep space blue, Deep gray, Ice blue, Silver white.
Sole primary accent color: Electric Blue / Cherenkov Blue.

Prohibited: Cheap rainbow gradients, cyberpunk purple/pink, excessive RGB, overt neon, cheap glow, game UI, tech templates, heavy HUDs, meaningless complex numbers, PPT charts.

Must have abundant black negative space to keep light, particles, and ice as visual focal points.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[5. Cinematic Cinematography]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Avoid static shots. Use cinematic visual language: Extreme Wide Shot, Macro Shot, Extreme Macro, Deep Space Fly Through, Orbital Camera, Long Lens, Dolly In/Out, Tracking Shot, Crash Zoom, Whip Pan, Parallax, Volumetric Camera, Micro-to-Macro, Continuous Camera Movement.

Emphasize scale transitions across: Universe → Galaxy → Star → Earth → Antarctica → Ice Sheet → Detector → Atom → Particle.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[6. Cosmic Section]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Space scenes must serve the concept that neutrinos originate from extreme environments: supernovae, black hole accretion disks, relativistic jets, AGNs, gravitational lensing, spacetime curvature.

Extract a fine blue neutrino trajectory from an immense cosmic event and follow it with the camera.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[7. Neutrino Penetrating Earth]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Camera rapidly approaches Earth from space. Earth turns semi-transparent, revealing crust, mantle, outer core, inner core. Neutrino passes straight through with volumetric light and realistic layering, exiting the opposite side.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[8. Why Difficult to Detect]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Contrast visually: photons hit/reflect/absorb; other particles interact; neutrinos pass right through. Repeat, leaving darkness and a faint blue point.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[9. Antarctic Ice Sheet]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Cinematic ice dive from space down into Antarctica's ice depth, showing real refraction, scattering, crystal structure, cracks, air bubbles, and volumetric light, plunging into total darkness before IceCube detectors light up one by one.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[10. IceCube as a Visual Icon]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Design as an architectural, temple-like, futuristic 3D detector grid spanning kilometers with strong scale contrasts.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[11. The Most Important Scientific VFX]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Neutrino enters ice; camera dives to extreme macro (ice → molecule → atom → nucleus). Neutrino interacts → charged particle created → travels faster than light in ice → Cherenkov blue light cone forms, illuminating surrounding ice crystals and triggering IceCube sensors.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[12. Blue Light and Detectors]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Detectors light up sequentially according to physical arrival times, producing faint blue halos as camera flies through.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[13. Abstracting Principles into Visuals]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Show Cherenkov light detection, recording 3D coordinates and arrival timestamps, organically synthesizing the reconstructed particle trajectory.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[14. Timing-Difference Localization]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Visualize wavefronts, timestamps, and 3D paths merging into a directional arrow extending back through ice, Earth, and space pointing to the distant cosmic origin (SOURCE RECONSTRUCTION).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[15. Final Cosmic Scale]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Camera pulls back from IceCube → Antarctica → Earth → Moon orbit → Solar System → Milky Way → deep cosmos, connecting the tiny blue point to the vast universe.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[16. Final Visual Climax]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Black void with blue neutrino trajectory branching into LIGHT, GRAVITATIONAL WAVES, NEUTRINOS. First two fade, highlighting NEUTRINOS, concluding with "A NEW WINDOW TO THE UNIVERSE".

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[17. Motion Design]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Utilize particle systems, point clouds, volumetric light, depth of field, motion blur, procedural animation, physics-based motion with inertia and easing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[18. SRT-Driven Timing]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

I will provide an SRT file as the sole time reference. Automatically determine shot durations, transitions, and pacing based on lyrics.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[19. Visual Rhythm]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Verse: mysterious, restrained.
Pre-chorus: accelerating particles and camera motion.
Chorus: grand, explosive blue light, massive detector grid.

Final chorus: cosmic scale release.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Cinematic modern sans-serif title design, emphasizing keywords (NEUTRINO, ICECUBE, 2 KM, CHERENKOV LIGHT, TIME, POSITION, DIRECTION, SOURCE) in white and ice blue with ample negative space.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[21. Scientific Accuracy]

Preserve scientific rigor: do not claim neutrinos are massless; do not depict neutrinos as ordinary photons; Cherenkov radiation comes from secondary charged particles traveling through ice.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
[22. Aesthetic Standards & Final Deliverables]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
